description: Crowd it and one sweep of ivory clears the road. Otherwise it grazes, wool to the ankles, a herd of one.
lore: Nothing else grazing this country comes near it for size: wool to the ankles, a shoulder above a grown person's head, ivory curved out far enough to clear a road. It is not hunting anything and never was. Nearly everything that has ever gone wrong between one of these and a person happened because the person stood too close for too long — the head comes round, one sweep, and the conversation is over.

Watch the spacing instead. It keeps a gap open on either side of itself, and it halts the way an animal halts when the animal ahead has halted. There is no animal ahead. [[characters/a6d7323d|Gunnar]], who shares his measurements with no one, still marks the one on his eastern round as a fixed point, the way other maps use hills — the hills out there having proved less dependable.

Bringing one down takes the knees first, then a long settling into the grass, and what is left fits in a closed hand: [[items/pale_bone_soulstone|a piece of ivory webbed with hairline breaks]]. Every one of them is a break it kept walking after — the tusks it sheds are snapped clean at the root by things it never once broke stride for. What the piece lends whoever carries it is exactly what the animal had. Not strength. The habit of continuing while damaged.
